Currently there's a bit of an issue of name squatting with the default subverse hierarchy. Currently, on that other website, there's a lot of failing trust in a lot of the moderation of many of the default subs. Disgruntled users, powerless to reform their favorite subs, have been forking off into similar named subs. For example SubGods then gets forked into newSubGods, and SubGodNews, and SubSaiyans etc....

Additionally on a lighter note you have subs like Superbowl which are originally founded for posting pictures of Superb Owls, but as much as I love pictures of superb owls, it really should be for The Super Bowl. Why do the owl fans get the name just because they were there first?

I was thinking, what if everything was assigned district when created. So for instance if I create /v/Superbowl my sub is assigned an address of voat.co/v/Superbowl/82slk3/. We're the only Superbowl in town and we post superb pictures of owls all year and then a football fan wants a sub for the up coming as well as past Super Bowls. He should be able to create a subverse of the same name and get an address of say voat.co/v/Superbowl/29xkj2 and post all the sport ball championship things he wants. Now a visitor to v/Superbowl could get a disambiguation page similar to Wikipedia with links to all districts of that subverse ordered by recent activity.

A disambiguation page is probably the simplest solution, but I have some fancier ideas. Provided a user is not currently subscribed to any of the subverses you could show an aggregation of all districts who's activity is over a predetermined threshold as well as list all districts in the side bar. Users can then check and uncheck what districts they want to see and be subscribed to. If a sub fall out of use and someone wants to pick it back up, you no longer need to got through a whole waiting period and then request for ownership. You can just start a new sub and as long as you're at least equally active you'll appear to new comers. This also means that when there is a large contingent of users dissatisfied with the direction of the current sub we no longer need silly and confusing subverse names for multiples of the same content.

Functionality could also be designed to better manage subscriptions to these similar subs (i.e. districts). Maybe there's a group of people that just wants to get away from the drama and only post links strictly on topic. Maybe I like the idea, but I also link the drama. Currently if I subscribe to both SubGods and SubGodNews my front page is going to be flooded with multiple duplicate links. In this instance comments, as well as the voat score, could then be aggregated for a user subscribing to both or multiple districts; improving the overall experience of a power user.

I might be making a mountain out of a molehill here as users already find ways to work around these problems. I just think there's a big opportunity to design voat to better cater to how people organize and consume content on boards in 2015.
